conclusion.interpretation: The prior 2.6–4.9-second matched penalty shrank to about0.63s with one-second TCP readiness. Full churn still delayed correct Deployment/Service creation by about0.69/0.91s. The observed client difference is below the one-second probe cadence, similar to the0.72s RBAC-only trial, and not isolated from DNS/sampling or the held-reconcile schedule. This bounded evidence does not establish a Service-specific reproducible additional client outage. It also does not prove zero subsecond impact.
limits: One full-Service-churn observation under the one-second probe; the other fault reproduced only RBAC churn.
Only readiness period changed in the experimental inputs; predicate, port, timeout, thresholds and workers stayed fixed. One second narrows, rather than eliminates, probe timing uncertainty.
No query in the fast full-churn trial addressed the brief stale Service IP; prior default-probe stale-IP refusals remain real and preserved.
Fresh-connection read-only probes; no persistent-session/write/transaction guarantees tested.
